recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中紅血球在薄區仍一個疊一個排成短鏈或堆疊（像一疊銅板），這就是錢串狀排列（rouleaux），提示血中有大量單株免疫球蛋白（M protein）。
features: Red cells stacked in short chains and linear aggregates (rouleaux) throughout the thin area of the smear
Individual red cells are normocytic and mostly normochromic
Few leukocytes: segmented neutrophils and small lymphocytes; no circulating plasma cells seen in this field
Faint bluish background staining is not clearly appreciable at this magnification
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low-to-medium power shows prominent rouleaux formation, with red cells arranged in stacked chains even in the thin area of the smear. Red cells are otherwise normocytic, and platelets appear adequate in number. Scattered neutrophils and lymphocytes are present, and no circulating plasma cells are identified in this field. Findings are suggestive of increased plasma proteins, such as a monoclonal paraprotein, and are consistent with plasma cell myeloma in the appropriate clinical context.

ddx.vs: Agglutination forms irregular, grape-like three-dimensional clumps without linear stacking and disperses with warming, whereas rouleaux forms coin-stack chains.
Overlapping red cells in the thick part of a smear mimic rouleaux, so rouleaux should be confirmed in the monolayer as seen here.
Polyclonal protein increase can cause similar rouleaux, so serum protein electrophoresis/immunofixation is needed to demonstrate a monoclonal protein.
